# CANDIDATE: REQUIRE_BEARISH_FILL_BAR_THRESHOLD_TUNE

**Filed:** 2026-08-20  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The current REQUIRE_BEARISH_FILL_BAR gate (requiring any bearish fill bar body) removes net-winning bear trades because it filters out too many winners relative to losers. By increasing the minimum body percentage threshold (to 0.10 or 0.15), we aim to retain more fat-tail winners (which likely exhibit strong bearish candles with large bodies) while filtering out more losers (which may have smaller bodies or be doji-like), thereby improving the net P&L of the gate.

## Mechanism

The gate REQUIRE_BEARISH_FILL_BAR (gates.py #7) currently checks that the fill bar is bearish (close < open) and has a body size (|close - open| / (high - low)) above a threshold. The current threshold is effectively 0.0 (any bearish body). We propose to test thresholds of 0.10 and 0.15 in separate experiments. The gate will only allow the trade to proceed if the fill bar's body percentage meets or exceeds the threshold. We will run Stage-1 backtests for both thresholds and select the one that maximizes net P&L while preserving anchor day winners.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The analysis assumes the same account size as the base engine (Safe-2: $2K, Bold-2: ~$1.65K). The gate removal of 33 trades netting +$917 IS (from the revalidation candidate REQUIRE_BEARISH_FILL_BAR_REVAL) was measured on the current engine (real fills, ITM-2, −7% cap, chandelier arm+5%/trail15%). Scaling to a $1K paper account would realize approximately 14% of that headline ($128.38).

2. **Sample bias:** The revalidation candidate [REQUIRE_BEARISH_FILL_BAR_REVAL] was evaluated on the full OPRA period (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) with 33 bear trades in the removed set. The sample size is small (33 trades) and the selection method is based on the gate firing. There is a risk of overfit because the gate was ratified on an old engine and the current engine has changed (managed exits, etc.). The sign-UNstable nature (helps one window but hurts two larger recent windows) indicates potential overfit to specific time periods.

3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no OOS test has been performed for the threshold change; we only have the IS result from the revalidation candidate for the boolean gate).

4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (the threshold change has not been tested on real-fills; we only have the boolean gate revalidation on real-fills).

5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: If the threshold is set too high, we may filter out too many winners, turning the gate into a net loser (similar to the current boolean gate but worse). 
   - Max drawdown: Could increase if we lose the ability to capture fat-tail winners during volatile periods.
   - Blow-up scenario: If the threshold is set too low (like 0.0) we already see a net winner set being removed; setting it too high may cause us to miss significant moves.

6. **Concentration:** From the revalidation candidate, the removed set (33 trades) had 13 winners and 20 losers. The top 2 dates (5/04 and 5/15) accounted for 59.8% of the VIX_MODERATE raw P&L in the bear high-confidence subset (from the V14E_BEAR_ONLY_GATE candidate, but note: this is a different set). However, for the specific set of 33 trades removed by the gate, we do not have concentration data. We note that the gate's removed set is not concentrated on the anchor days (since the gate is near-vacuous on anchors). We will need to measure concentration in the Stage-1 backtest.

## Pre-merge gate

- Gym validators: 97/98 PASS (must re-run for the new threshold)
- Walk-forward: WF ≥ 0.70 (OOS test required)
- Real-fills: Validate on top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04) to ensure no anchor regression and retention of winners

## Confidence

3 / 10 -- We have no data on the effect of changing the threshold to 0.10 or 0.15. The current boolean gate (threshold=0.0) is known to remove a net-winner set, but we do not know if a higher threshold would improve the net P&L of the gate. We are proposing based on the hypothesis that winners have stronger bodies.
